xref.title: Nash the Slash (Jeff Plunman, Toronto, 1948–2014) – Surgical Bandages Adopted After Three Mile Island Accident (1979); David Gilmour Offered Guitar Part but Nash Refused All Guitars
xref.body: Nash the Slash's real name was Jeff Plunman, born in Toronto on March 26, 1948. The stage name came from a character in a 1927 Laurel and Hardy silent film. He co-founded the prog band FM in 1975 and audiences could see his face briefly, but after the nuclear accident at Three Mile Island near Harrisburg, Pennsylvania in March 1979, Nash adopted surgical bandages that completely obscured his face as a way of raising awareness about what could happen if a nuclear plant melted down. He left FM around 1980 to resume his solo career, toured with Gary Numan and the Tubes, hung out with Iggy Pop and Daniel Lanois, and Brian Eno collaborated on his records. David Gilmour of Pink Floyd was such a fan that he offered to lay down a guitar part on one of Nash's songs — but Nash refused because he never used guitars on any of his songs. He made records until 2012, was especially popular in Germany and Poland, and died of an apparent heart attack at his Toronto home on May 10, 2014, at age 66. His music and costumes are managed by the Nash the Slash Legacy organization and much was donated to the National Music Center in Calgary. His best-known record was 1984's American Bandages. "David Gilmore of Pink Floyd was such a fan that he offered to lay down a guitar part on one of Nash's songs, but Nash refused because he never, ever used guitars on any of his songs."

xref.title: 1992 Overdose and Cardiac Arrest
xref.body: In September 1992, while on tour with Metallica, Slash was staying in San Francisco before an Oakland gig. After the Oakland show, drug dealers came to his hotel room at 5 a.m., and Slash took a powerful speedball (heroin and cocaine). He collapsed in the hallway due to cardiac arrest and was technically dead for eight minutes. Paramedics revived him with an adrenaline needle. He was transported to the hospital but quickly signed himself out and was back on stage in Los Angeles two days later. "he'd been technically dead for eight minutes due to cardiac arrest."

xref.title: Bangkok Concert Self-Harm (April 23, 1994)
xref.body: During a concert in Bangkok, a fan sent miniature ceremonial swords backstage with a request for Richie Edwards to slash himself on stage. Richie complied, inflicting visible wounds across his chest, stating, "The fan asked me to. I didn't want to let him down." "When the band explained Bangkok on April 23, 1994, a fan sent some miniature ceremonial swords backstage with a note asking Richie to slash himself on stage. Which he did."

xref.title: Black Calvarros Restaurant, Paris (2006) – Rock Music Bar Near the Four Seasons, Closed After Two Years
xref.body: Cornell opened a high-end restaurant in Paris called Black Calvarros in 2006, located across from the Four Seasons hotel about five blocks from the Champs-Élysées. During renovations, a ceiling fresco dating to the 1780s was discovered. The joint venture with his wife Vicki and brother-in-law DJ Nick Blast offered food including caramelized quail, truffled mac and cheese, and gourmet hot dogs. Interior design was by the designer of the annual Victoria's Secret Fashion Show. The restaurant sometimes did not close until 7am but shut down after a couple of years. "A restaurant slash bar where you could go in Paris to hear rock music."
